newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Firmer amid gains in crude values.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Firmer amid gains in crude values.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market staged firmer on Friday in line with gains in crude values, traders said.
Trading interest also improved after the market's falls earlier this week, they said.
The 180-cst grade was traded at $97.50 per tonne for August 11-15 lifting, up from Thursday's $95.5 traded level.
Interest was also seen in the 380-cst grade, which was traded at $94 per tonne earlier this week, but no deals were heard done.
Traders said prices are likely to stay within range and they did not expect any significant price movements.
"Demand is just normal but supplies are quite sufficient at the moment. Prices (for 180-cst) can not exceed $100 in the near term," said one trader.
Another traders noted firm fuel oil markets in other regions, saying the Singapore market should be supported.
Fuel oil swaps firmed slightly also on back of firmer overnight crude values and on intermonth spread trading.
August was last quoted at $98/$98.75 and September at $98.00/$99.00 from Thursday's $97.75/$98.50 for both months.
No transaction was reported on SIMEX fuel oil futures contract on late Friday.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
